banks.name: Federal Reserve
banks.priced: Oct 28: HELD at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote (Cook + Hammack dissented for a +25bp hike); activity upgraded to 'strong' from 'solid', inflation 'remains elevated', no explicit December commitment in the text. December: hike ~78% in the morning (CME FedWatch via Reuters Oct 29, down from ~84% pre-decision), ~83% after the Oct 29 GDP/PCE block (FedWatch via SmartXSignals Oct 29), ~75% into Oct 30 Europe (FedWatch via FXStreet Oct 30, down from 84.2% a day prior). Next meeting Dec 8-9 with SEP/dot plot. Oct 30 US session: Musalem (voter) wants a hike 'again soon' — policy still accommodative; Logan: 'at least two more' 25bp hikes, then a pause. Pricing trimmed anyway: ~70% Dec hike (Prime Terminal via FXStreet Oct 30), down from 84% after the Oct 28 meeting — the tech sell-off pulled yields lower (10Y ~4.94%). Nov 2 Asia: Dec hike ~72% (futures via Stockbiz) to ~75% (NordFX) — steady vs ~70% at the Oct 30 close. Nov 2: total tightening priced ~55bp, down from >70bp a month ago (Stockbiz); Dec hike ~72%. Nov 3 morning: Dec hike ~75% (CME FedWatch via Cointime; Kalshi ~73%) — steady vs Nov 2. Nov 3 US session: Dec hike 78.9% (CME FedWatch via TradingView/SeekingAlpha, up from 74.4% Monday) after the JOLTS beat (7.523M) and factory orders beat (+1.8%); 10Y touched 4.97%. Nov 4 US session: Dec hike ~82.6% (CME FedWatch via Reuters NY, up from 77.4% prior session; Barchart ~83%) despite the dollar slide — the midterm sweep moved FX more than rate pricing; 10Y eased to ~4.92% (from the Nov 3 4.97% touch). ADP beat (+86K) and ISM services small miss (54.5) roughly offset into Friday payrolls. Nov 5 Tokyo: Dec hike 81.2% for at least 25bp (CME FedWatch via Reuters), vs ~82.6% in the Nov 4 US session — pricing essentially steady after the sweep. Nov 5 morning: Dec hike ~80.7-81.2% (CME FedWatch via Reuters — 80.7% NY, 81.2% Tokyo), essentially steady vs ~82.6% Nov 4; 10Y ~4.85% (lowest since Sep 10, Reuters). Claims 7:30am CT (fcst 197K) + payrolls Fri (FF fcst +65K) are the next inputs. Nov 5 US session: Dec hike ~80% (CME FedWatch reads 79-82%, vs 81.2% this morning) after the 7:30am CT triple beat (claims 189K, productivity +3.6%, ULC -0.7%); 10Y ~4.89%, 2Y ~4.51% into the close. Payrolls Fri 7:30am CT (consensus ~+60K, unemployment 4.2%) is the next test of the hike bet. Nov 6 Asia: Dec hike ~68% (CME FedWatch via Reuters), down from ~80% Nov 5 US session and 81.2% Nov 5 morning — the AI/data-center equity rout pulled yields lower (10Y ~4.84%, 2Y ~4.47% in Asia) and the haven bid went to JPY/CHF, not the dollar; payrolls 7:30am CT (fcst 65K) is the next test of the hike bet. Nov 6 7:30am CT: payrolls BEAT +165K (vs 65K fcst; Sep revised to +60K, Aug to +186K), unemployment 4.1%, AHE +0.4% m/m (+3.1% y/y); DXY jumped to 102.20 (+0.62%) — the beat re-arms the December hike case ahead of Tuesday's CPI. Nov 6 US session: Dec hike ~77% (CME FedWatch via Reuters/Invezz, up from ~67% Thu) after the +165K payrolls beat; 2Y 4.53%, 10Y ~4.87% at the close; UoM sentiment beat 51.0, 1-yr inflation expectations cooled to 4.3%. Next test: Oct CPI Tue Nov 10. Nov 7: Dec hike ~77% holding into the weekend (Kalshi 76.5-78%, Polymarket 76.5%, CME futures 76.1%, as of ~1-2pm ET); Williams (NY Fed) Fri: growth 'remarkably resilient', inflation too high, 'essential' to bring it back to 2%. Nov 8: Dec hike ~75.5-77% holding into Tuesday's CPI (CME FedWatch ~75.5% as of Nov 8; Kalshi 76.5-78%, Polymarket 76.5%, CME futures 76.1% Nov 7) — essentially flat over the weekend. Nov 9: Dec hike ~79% (Reuters/CME FedWatch, up from 71% a week earlier) — the +165K payrolls beat held through the weekend; Tuesday's Oct CPI (7:30am CT) is the next test. Nov 9 London: Dec hike ~81% (Reuters/CME FedWatch, up from ~79% in Asia; MarketWatch 80.5%) — payrolls beat + AI-rout pause into Tuesday's CPI; Williams/Musalem/Daly Fri all backed further hikes. Nov 9 NY close: Dec hike ~82% (Reuters/CME FedWatch via Kitco, up from ~81% London; ~76% on some trackers) into Tuesday's Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y); 2Y 4.54%, 10Y 4.87%. $58B 3Y auction tailed WI by 0.5bp (biggest since May), BTC 2.53 — weakest of 2026, indirects 55.5% (soft foreign demand), directs record 35.0%. Nov 10 Asia: Dec hike ~80% (rate-futures pricing via HDFC Sky; Reuters/CME FedWatch ~82% Nov 9 NY) — holding ~80-82% after the +165K payrolls beat; today's Oct CPI (7:30am CT, fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y) is the next test. FRED confirms the target range 3.75-4.00% (Nov 7). NY Fed Oct survey (Nov 9): inflation expectations flat at 3.9% (1y) / 3.3% (3y) / 3.0% (5y); jobless-rate expectations highest since April 2020. Nov 10 London: Waller (BoE Watchers Conference, London) leans +25bp in Dec even if Oct CPI cools — and says a 50bp move should be considered if core CPI prints ~0.3% or higher ('hiking only 25bp would put our credibility at risk'). Dec hike now fully priced: ~95.6% (CME FedWatch via BigGo) to ~99% (investingLive), up from ~82% Nov 9 NY; 2Y +6bp to ~4.61%, 10Y ~4.88%. The Oct CPI print (7:30am CT) is now the 25bp-vs-50bp test. Nov 10 7:30am CT: Oct CPI HOT — headline +0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% fcst), core +0.3% (vs +0.2%) — core hits Waller's 50bp trigger exactly, but the market did NOT price 50bp: CME FedWatch (07:20 CT, pre-print) +25bp 98.8%, 50bp 0.0%; post-print Investing.com monitor (~08:35 ET) +25bp 98.2%, hold 1.8%. DXY ~101.9. Dec stays a +25bp hike in the market's eyes. Nov 10 US session: post-CPI pricing — Dec hike effectively certain (~100% for at least 25bp); CME FedWatch afternoon reads split ~85.3% for +25bp / 14.7% for +50bp (tradingkey 15:00Z; InvestingLive ~12% for 50bp), while an earlier FXStreet read had ~99% for 25bp (14:15Z) — snapshots differ, the hike itself is not in doubt; Reuters poll of 101 economists (Nov 6-10) unanimous for +25bp on Dec 9. 2Y 4.76% (+21bp), 10Y 5.02% (+15bp, back above 5.00%). $42B 10Y auction soft: high yield 5.020%, BTC 2.46 (below the 2.60 six-auction avg), indirects 61.2% (vs 80.3% Oct), dealers 9.8%. Nov 11 Asia: CME FedWatch firms — 25bp 91.9% (up from 84% a day earlier), 50bp 9.1%, pause fully priced out; better-than-even odds of a second hike in Jan (Reuters Asia wrap, Nov 11 00:56Z). Philly Fed President Paulson: Oct CPI “shows that inflationary pressures remain clearly evident”. Dallas Fed President Logan: the Fed “needs to implement at least two more rate increases, each by 25 basis points” and may need to raise faster this winter. Reuters poll of 101 economists (Nov 6-10) unanimous for +25bp Dec 9. Nov 11 London: DXY pushes to a four-week high (~102.4-102.53) as the CPI beat + hawkish Fed talk digest; FedWatch 25bp ~85% (Reuters 09:15Z update) vs 91.9% in Asia (00:56Z) — the 50bp tail widened a touch; the Dec hike itself remains essentially certain; US bond market closed for Veterans Day, so 2Y/10Y stay at Tuesday's close (4.73%/4.98%). Nov 11 London: DXY pushes to a four-week high (~102.4-102.53) as the CPI beat + hawkish Fed talk digest; FedWatch 25bp ~85% (Reuters 09:15Z update) vs 91.9% in Asia (00:56Z) — the 50bp tail widened a touch; the Dec hike itself remains essentially certain; US bond market closed for Veterans Day, so 2Y/10Y stay at Tuesday's close (4.73%/4.98%). Nov 11 NY close: Dec 25bp ~87% (CME FedWatch via Reuters) vs ~85% in London and ~70% a month ago; the 50bp tail ~13%; the hike itself essentially certain; better-than-even odds of a second hike in Jan. US bond market closed for Veterans Day — 2Y/10Y stay at Tuesday's close (4.73%/4.98%). Nov 12 Asia: Dec hike ~87% 25bp / ~13% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Reuters, Nov 11 NY session) — unchanged overnight. Deutsche Bank now sees three hikes (Dec, Jan, Mar); UBS two (Dec, Mar); Goldman another early next year. NY Fed President Williams speaks on a panel late Thu — 'any guidance will be seized on' (NAB). US bond market reopens today after Veterans Day — 2Y ~4.77%, 10Y ~4.99%.

banks.detail: October a hold at ~84-85% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21; Kalshi hold 89%) — blackout confirmed, no Fed speakers. December hike ~90%. 20-yr auction (Oct 21): $13B at 5.469% — record high since the tenor's May-2020 reintroduction; tailed WI 5.460% by 0.9bp (4th tail in a row, improved on Sept's 2bp); B/C 2.73 (vs 2.57 Sept); indirects 58.2% (avg 65.2% — soft foreign demand); directs record 31.6%. Dow Jones/WSJ: 'softer-than-expected'; Barron's: little market reaction. 10Y 5.12%, 2Y 4.79% (FRED DGS10/DGS2, Oct 20). The housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs the hot inflation week (import prices +8.1% y/y). Friday: 10Y 4.994% (baystreet, Oct 23) — steadied after Thursday's 19.5bp plunge; Dec-hike pricing eased to ~80% (FXStreet, Oct 23). Friday close: 10Y 5.00% (+4bp), 2Y 4.69% (marketbriefer) — yields reversed part of Thursday's 19.5bp haven plunge on hot PMIs + oil. Hyperscaler earnings share the tape with the FOMC: Alphabet + Microsoft Wed after the close, Amazon Thu. Oct 27 (FXEmpire): DXY near a one-week high ~102.04 as five central-bank decisions in three days plus the UK Budget keep traders cautious; CME Dec-hike odds ~73% (Monday) vs ~80%+ last week. Oct 28: HELD 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike). Warsh presser: 2Y pulled back to 4.726% (-1bp), 10Y 5.007% (+1bp); DXY slipped to ~102.05 off its two-week high; stocks +0.2% (Reuters/Forex.com: Warsh fell short of a full hawkish December hint). December hike ~86% CME post-decision.
banks.summary: The Fed held in October (10-2, two hawkish dissents) and left December open; markets price a December hike as essentially certain — 25bp ~85% (Nov 11, CME FedWatch via Reuters), after 91.9% in Asia. Recent inflation has run hot, which keeps the dollar supported while markets wait.

banks.name: Bank of Canada
banks.priced: Oct 28: HIKED +25bp to 2.50%, first hike since July 2023, as expected; MPR lifts 2027 inflation to 3.1% (from 2.0%), inflation back to 2% only by mid-2028; Macklem: further hikes possible but Council will 'proceed carefully'. December: further hike ~45% (swaps via Reuters); a second hike fully discounted by January. Loonie +0.1% to 1.4035 post-decision; Can 2Y hit a 2-year high 3.441%. Nov 3: Macklem (finance committee) restated “could be a need to raise further” but proceed carefully, one meeting at a time; CPI seen ~3.5% by year-end, at/above 3% through much of 2027, near 2% by mid-2028. December further-hike ~56% (investinglive Nov 3), up from ~45% at the Oct 28 decision. Nov 5: Macklem (Senate committee) — Oct 28 hike meant to stop Canadians getting 'hit twice'; 'there could be a need to raise further, but... proceed carefully,' one meeting at a time; January outlook will reflect today's budget. Dec further-hike ~56% (Nov 3 read). Nov 6 7:30am CT: Canada jobs MISSED — employment -4.7K (vs +14.6K fcst), unemployment 6.7% (from 6.5%); USD/CAD ~1.4100; the miss questions the December further-hike case (~56% Nov 3 read). Nov 6 US session: USD/CAD ~1.4101 at the close after the jobs miss and the US payrolls beat; Ivey PMI small beat 58.3. Nov 7: second Dec hike ~35% (LSEG), down from the ~56% Nov 3 read, after the jobs miss. Nov 8: swaps-implied Dec hike ~32% (FinancialJuice via CryptoBriefing / ForexPulse Nov 6, down from 40% pre-jobs) and OIS 36.4% (Nov 7) — the ~35% LSEG read confirmed; hold now the base case (Polymarket 'no change' ~73%). Nov 9 London: USD/CAD ~1.4078 as the dollar gives back; BoC Market Participants Survey due today. Nov 10: Summary of Deliberations (Oct 28 decision) — Council debated hold (2.25%) vs hike and chose 2.50%; energy “higher for longer” with cost pass-through building; CPI seen 3.5% end-2026, above 3% through much of 2027, back to 2% by mid-2028; growth revised up (2026 to 1%, 2027-28 to 2%). Dec further-hike ~32-36% (swaps/OIS), hold still the base case — the minutes confirm the Oct 28 message rather than extending it. Nov 12 Asia: WTI ~$85.49 gives back Wednesday's gains; EIA today 10:30am CT. Dec further-hike ~32-36%, hold the base case.

banks.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand
banks.priced: Oct 28: HELD at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote vs ~85-95% hike pricing (Bloomberg 85%, finimize 89%, Dow Jones ~95%; Reuters poll 22/27 economists expected a hike). All members agreed further tightening is likely; Breman raised restrictive territory; ANZ sees Dec/Feb/Mar hikes to 3.50%. Next decision Dec 9. Nov 5: markets price <50% chance of a Dec 9 hike, down from ~75% earlier this week after the Q3 jobs miss (unemployment 5.7%, 11-year high); NZ parliamentary elections Fri 3:45pm CT. NZ parliamentary elections Fri 3:45pm CT — result lands overnight; Dec 9 hike still priced <50%. Nov 7: NZ election preliminary count — no clear winner (National 42 seats, Labour 36; National+ACT+NZ First 67 seats, a bare majority); official result Nov 27 after special votes; coalition talks to follow. Nov 9 London: kiwi +1.0% to $0.5602 — strongest major as risk rebounds; official result Nov 27. Nov 12 Asia: kiwi ~$0.5559 (-0.23%); official election result Nov 27.

banks.summary: The RBNZ surprised markets by holding at 2.75% on October 28 in a 4-3 vote — but it was a hawkish hold: every member agreed further tightening is likely, and December 9 is live.

banks.name: European Central Bank
banks.priced: Oct 29: HELD at 2.50% (deposit; main refi 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%) as expected (Reuters poll 70/73 for hold); statement data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting, no pre-commitment. Lagarde presser: the direction of travel is 'clear' and a hike was debated but unanimously deferred to December; Reuters sources: a Dec 17 hike is now 'all but certain', with a pause thereafter as higher yields bite (ECB estimates: the yield rise cuts 2027-28 growth ~100bp and inflation ~90bp). Same morning, Lagarde announced she steps down Feb 7, 2027, nine months early; succession starts immediately. December: hike ~86%+ (64/73 economists in the Reuters poll; market ~84-88% pre-decision). France: OAT-Bund ~167-177bp; S&P reviews France Nov 27. Nov 4: Dec hike ~89% (Barchart/CME) after the inline Oct flash CPI (4.0% y/y, core 2.5%) — no fresh impulse, hike case intact. Nov 5: Lagarde (Milan) — 'many indicators between now and December' will determine whether a hike is necessary; 4% inflation 'predominantly energy'; tools still needed to avoid inflation running away. No new commitment; Dec hike ~89% intact. Nov 6: Lane — inflation must return to target 'within a year or two', financial conditions already tightened; 'gather information between now and December'. EZ retail sales missed (-0.7% m/m). Dec hike ~89% intact. Nov 9 London: EUR/USD ~$1.1187 (+0.4%) as the dollar eases; Dec hike ~89% intact; Lagarde speaks Thu 1:30pm CT. Nov 11: German CPI final 2.8% y/y for Oct, confirming the preliminary — no fresh impulse; Dec hike ~89% intact; Lagarde at the Paris Peace Forum (09:45Z) with no new policy signal in major-wire coverage. Nov 11 NY close: Lagarde's Paris Peace Forum remarks carried no policy signal; Dec hike ~89-92% (morning briefing 92%); EUR/USD ~1.1096, lowest since May 2025. Lagarde speaks again Thu 1:30pm CT. Nov 12 Asia: Dec hike ~92% intact — no new read; Lagarde speaks again Thu 1:30pm CT; EZ GDP (2nd est.) Fri 4:00am CT.

banks.detail: October-29 hold virtually certain — Reuters Oct-8 poll: 70 of 73 economists expect a hold at 2.50%. December hike ~76% (ECB Watch, ~Oct-15 vintage; the earlier ~88% poll read is stale) — Commerzbank: 'market is pricing in one [hike] for December and slightly more than one additional hike by mid-2027'. Lagarde: no major-wire carry of new rate remarks indexed today. German PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%); EZ final CPI 3.8% confirmed. Eurozone natural gas >EUR 90/MWh (first since Dec 2022) — fresh energy-cost pressure. France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); OAT 4.948% (+2.9bp, WSJ/Tradeweb); OAT-Bund ~153bp; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 negative — markets expect a one-notch cut to A1). EUR/USD 1.1233, flat. IMF (Oct 16 regular Europe report): at least one further 25bp ECB hike in 2026 is warranted to keep core inflation contained; 'further tightening likely warranted' beyond 2026. https://www.reuters.com/business/imf-expects-least-one-more-25-bps-ecb-rate-hike-2026-2026-10-16/ Friday: France 10Y 5.14% (highest since July 2002); OAT-Bund 170-177bp (highest since 2011); Moody's reviews France (Aa3 neg) after the US close (~3pm CT) — downgrade priced in, outlook the variable (Reuters). Panetta: yield climb a growth headwind, not a crisis (baystreet). Flash PMIs all missed — France comp 48.4 back in contraction. Moody's decision (Oct 23 evening): Aa3 affirmed with negative outlook — the downgrade to A1 that most economists expected did not come; the agency wants a deficit-cutting 2027 budget and sees French debt topping 120% of GDP in 2027; S&P next reviews France Nov 27. Newsquawk: the Oct-29 statement may be 'even more non-committal than typical'; growing chatter about Lagarde's departure as a presser talking point. Oct 29 outcome: held at 2.50% as expected; Lagarde signaled the December direction clearly and announced her Feb 7, 2027 departure; Reuters sources call a Dec 17 hike all but certain.
banks.summary: The ECB held in October and leans toward a December hike, with euro-area inflation at a three-year high (4.0% y/y); German CPI final confirmed 2.8% for October. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

banks.name: Bank of Japan
banks.priced: Oct 30: HELD at 1.25% (8-1; Takata dissented for 1.50%); Outlook Report judged underlying inflation 'generally consistent' with the 2% target, FY2027 core CPI median raised to 2.6% (from 2.4%); ETF sales accelerated to ~¥860B/yr from Jan 2027. December: hike ~80% (OIS per Nikkei; Reuters poll: ~80% of economists naming a month chose December). Ueda presser 1:30am CT. Nov 5: September minutes reinforced December hike bets (Reuters Tokyo); USD/JPY ~158.0-158.25 Asia. Nov 5 US session: yen strongest of the day (USD/JPY 157.82, -0.38%) as the tech-led equity selloff drove haven demand on top of the hawkish September minutes; Ueda speaks Fri 10:00am CT. Nov 6: Ueda — real rates 'have not risen significantly' (BBX) — no pushback on the ~80% Dec hike; former BoJ chief economist Kameda expects Dec to 1.50%, then quarterly to a 2% terminal. Nov 9: MoF data confirms Japan spent a record $50bn in a single day (Jul 30) defending the yen, ~$97bn across Jul–Aug incl. the first joint intervention with the US since 1998 (WSJ) — intervention history is live context with USD/JPY ~158.3; BoJ Summary of Opinions tonight 5:50pm CT. Nov 9 London: USD/JPY ~157.99 as the dollar gives back Friday's jump; BoJ Summary of Opinions tonight 5:50pm CT. Nov 9 NY close: USD/JPY ~158.01 as the dollar softens; BoJ Summary of Opinions tonight 5:50pm CT; Dec hike ~80% intact. Nov 10: Summary of Opinions (Oct 29-30) released 8:50 JST — several members want the next hike 'without becoming overly cautious' and to 'step up the pace' toward neutral, seen 'considerably above 1%' by one member; doves warn the rate is already in the estimated neutral range (1.1-2.5%) and a further hike could weigh on the economy; core CPI seen above 3% into year-end. Reuters poll: Dec to 1.50%, quarterly pace, terminal 1.75-2%; Dec hike ~80% intact; USD/JPY ~157.98 after the release. Nov 10: Summary of Opinions (Oct 29-30) hawkish — several members want the next hike 'without becoming overly cautious' / to 'step up the pace' toward neutral, seen 'considerably above 1%'; doves warn the rate is already in the estimated neutral range (1.1-2.5%). Reuters poll: Dec to 1.50%, quarterly pace, terminal 1.75-2%. Dec hike ~80% intact; USD/JPY ~158.1 after Waller's remarks. Nov 11 London: USD/JPY pushes toward 160, the yen's weakest in ~7 weeks, as the dollar extends its CPI gains; Dec hike ~80% intact; Japan PPI tonight 5:50pm CT (fcst 6.5% y/y). Nov 11 NY close: USD/JPY 159.8-159.83, strongest in over two months, closing on 160; Dec hike ~84% (morning briefing pricing) vs ~80%; Japan PPI tonight 5:50pm CT (fcst 6.5% y/y). December hike ~80% (Japan Times/Bloomberg, Oct 21, via ex-BoJ executive Maeda, who expects Dec then Mar/Apr) — a step up from the ~73-74% read. Ueda's 'quite close' to 2% leans December, not October. banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December — the Summary of Opinions was hawkish and December is ~80% priced. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen; USD/JPY pushes toward 160 meanwhile.

Bullock presser: no guidance - 'probably good to take stock', the hike 'may not be enough' but 'not as obvious'; market pricing has the cash rate still around 4.8% at end-2027 (RBA SMP summaries). Next decision Dec 8. Pre-decision pricing was ~81% for the hike (ActionForex 81.2%; ASX-futures model 70.8%). Nov 5: Hauser (Canberra) — 'inflation is too high, whichever measure you use'; public confidence in the RBA's inflation fight eroding (Reuters); denied his October remarks were aimed at swaying the board; AUD unmoved (~$0.7013, FXStreet). Nov 5 US session: AUD/USD 0.6935 (-1.02%), the day's weakest major, on the tech-led risk-off slide and the dovish read of Tuesday's hike; Citi stays bearish (target 0.6660). Australia Sep trade surplus widened to A$2.826B. Nov 6: AUD/USD ~0.6857 at the close (-1.12%), weakest major again on the payrolls beat + risk-off tape. Nov 9 London: AUD/USD ~$0.6899 (+0.5%) as the AI rout pauses and risk rebounds. Nov 12 Asia: Aussie ~$0.6847, near a 32-week low; Dec 8 decision next.

banks.detail: November 2-3 hike ~42% — LSEG via Marthio (Oct 21); OIS 41-55% post-Hauser; Goldman Sachs flipped to a November-hike call (25bp to 4.85%, 'the fifth of 2026'); CBA/ANZ a coin toss; Westpac expects 4.85%. Hauser called the inflation outlook 'materially worse' (in part on high oil) — the hawkish follow-through repriced Nov from ~30% at week's start. AUD/USD 0.7032 (+0.2-0.3%), a 3-week high. Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot. China LPR held for the 17th straight month (1y 3.00%, 5y 3.50%); PBoC to run daily overnight reverse repos Oct 21-Nov 2 (up to ¥1T/day) — first step toward an overnight policy rate. Hauser (Oct 20): inflation outlook 'materially worse' — Q3 trimmed expected above the Bank's 0.8% q/q forecast (consensus 1.0% q/q); Goldman Sachs tipped to a November hike absent a downside CPI surprise; another rise fully priced by March. Oct 28: Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's August path — trimmed +1.0% q/q vs the Bank's 0.8% forecast, Q3 trimmed 3.7% y/y, monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y vs 4.2% exp — Nov hike odds jumped to ~79-85%. Nov 3: RBA HIKED +25bp to 4.85% (6-3, three for hold), fifth hike of 2026, highest since Dec 2008; SMP revised the inflation path materially higher (headline 4.5% Dec 2026 vs 3.6% in August forecasts; 3.7% June 2027 vs 2.8%) and pushed return to the top of the 2-3% band to late 2027. Bullock: no guidance on the next move. AUD fell to $0.6974 after the decision despite the hike. Next decision Dec 8.
banks.summary: The RBA hiked to 4.85% on November 3 in a split 6-3 vote - the fifth rise of 2026 and the highest cash rate since December 2008 - but Bullock gave no guidance on what comes next, and the Aussie slipped below $0.70 on the decision.

banks.name: Bank of England
banks.priced: Nov 5: hike ~94.4% (ActionForex Nov 2; OIS ~90%; post-CPI ~96-97%, Oct 21-23); December back-to-back ~48-61%. Healey's first Budget lands Wednesday — 8 days before the decision (newsquawk: CGT rise off the table, banks face £2-5B tax rise). Budget delivered Oct 28: headroom £15B, 10Y gilt -2bp to 5.323%, GBP $1.3298 — the 'boring budget' bond markets wanted (Reuters/XTB). Nov 2: Goldman now expects a Feb hike too (after Thu's); LSEG ~92% for Thu (vs 94.4% ActionForex). Nov 4: pricing firmed to ~96.7% for the Nov 5 hike to 4.00% (Morningstar derivatives Nov 2; ~96% MoneyToTheMasses; ActionForex 94.4% Nov 2); Healey's Budget delivered Oct 28 (headroom £15B in 2029/30). ING expects a 7-2 vote with a February follow-up likely; Reuters poll 54/63 economists expect 4.00%. Nov 5: HIKED +25bp to 4.00% (8-1; Mann dissented for +50bp to 4.25%) — first hike since Aug 2023, as expected; no hold dissenters (Dhingra/Taylor voted for the hike). Bailey: 'Today's increase shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes. But unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase.' Lombardelli: further hike likely in the near term; Greene/Pill: 'further tightening'/'additional hikes'; Dhingra/Taylor: need stronger evidence of second-round effects. MPR: CPI seen near 5% by mid-2027. GBP/USD steady ~$1.347 after the decision. Next decision Dec 17; markets pricing three to four more hikes through 2027. Bailey (presser): not necessarily the first of a series, but the case for another 25bp is 'fairly strong' if the US–Iran conflict stays unresolved; the MPC would have hiked even knowing the oil moves of the prior 48 hours. Nov 6: GBP/USD ~1.3361 at the close (-0.79%) as the dollar jumped on US payrolls — sterling's biggest daily drop since Sep 23. Nov 9 NY close: Bailey spoke in Zurich (Swiss Institute of International Studies) — AI as an early positive supply shock (nearly a fifth of UK GDP growth since early 2026), warned of an 'AI asset price bubble', stressed central-bank independence; no new December steer. GBP/USD ~$1.3415 (+0.40%). UK GDP Thu 1:00am CT (Q3 +0.7% q/q fcst). Nov 10: Deputy Gov Lombardelli (Guardian interview) 'wouldn't rule out' a December hike — keeps a mild hawkish bias alive into the Dec 17 decision; GBP/USD ~1.3425 after Waller's dollar lift (from a 1.3459 London high). Nov 11 London: GBP/USD ~$1.332, near a two-week low as the dollar extends its CPI gains; UK GDP Thu 1:00am CT (Q3 +0.7% q/q fcst) is the next domestic test. Nov 11 NY close: Dec back-to-back hike ~67% (morning briefing pricing) vs the 48-61% range; GBP/USD ~1.3284, near a two-week low; UK GDP Thu 1:00am CT (Q3 +0.7% q/q fcst) is the next domestic test. Nov 12 Asia: UK Q3 GDP prints 1:00am CT today (fcst +0.7% q/q, Sep +0.0% m/m) — first growth read since the hike to 4.00%; Dec back-to-back ~67%.

banks.detail: November-5 hike ~95-98% to 4.00% (centralbank.watch 95.1%; deVere 98%; AJ Bell: 'nearing 100%' post-CPI). December back-to-back 51.2% (+12.8bp priced, centralbank.watch) — AJ Bell sees '>50% chance' of a year-end second hike. Bailey's 8am CT fireside: zero major-wire carry of new rate-policy remarks (headline-only: would not discuss monetary policy) — below bar. UK labor beat stands: unemp 4.7% (lowest since mid-2025), wages 3.7%. Greene hawkish: wage disinflation 'has stalled at levels above those consistent with inflation at 2%.' ING: BoE to hike Nov + Feb, then pause. Healey's first Budget Oct 28. Nov 5 outcome: HIKED +25bp to 4.00% (8-1; Mann for +50bp); first hike since Aug 2023. Bailey presser 6:30am CT: not necessarily the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved. MPR: CPI near 5% by mid-2027. GBP/USD ~$1.347 post-decision (Reuters).
banks.summary: The Bank of England hiked to 4.00% on November 5 in an 8-1 vote — its first rise since August 2023 — with Mann dissenting for a bigger 50bp move. Bailey said it is unlikely to be the last hike unless the Middle East conflict is resolved, and the Bank sees CPI near 5% by mid-2027; sterling ~$1.332 in London, near a two-week low.
